contributions.note: ESCALATED AND DECIDED BY ARITHMETIC, NOT BY GLYPH. A 1200 dpi crop of this cell renders the four characters '2500' with the decimal point buried in the 5's tail, i.e. it could be read 2,500.00. It is 25.00: with 25.00 the page's own printed 'Subtotal for this page' closes EXACTLY at 3,014.00, and Schedule A's printed Total (7,034.00), the cover's Column A and the balance ladder's close (493.18) all close with it; a 2,500.00 reading would break all four printed figures at once. Per GOTCHAS ('ARITHMETIC CLOSURE OUTRANKS GLYPH READING', the Rhodes reversal), the sum decides and the glyph is preserved here verbatim as written: '2500' with no visible point

contributions.detail: THE PAGE-SUBTOTAL GATE PASSES ON EVERY SHEET. p3's 17 rows sum to 2,685.00 = its printed 'Subtotal for this page'; p4's 17 rows sum to 1,335.00 = its printed subtotal; p5's 17 rows sum to 3,014.00 = its printed subtotal. 2,685.00 + 1,335.00 + 3,014.00 = 7,034.00 = the printed 'Total Contributions Received' on all three sheets = the cover's promoted PER-PERIOD Column A cell = summary line 4 'Total Contributions Received (From Line 1 Column A)' = line 5 'Subtotal' (line 3, Balance at Beginning, is a struck ZERO GLYPH). Column B 'Year-to-Date Total' prints 7,553.48 and is NOT summed as an increment; it is exactly this period's 7,034.00 plus the 519.48 this filer reported in June, i.e. the cumulative column behaving as the promotion regime describes. ONE ROW WAS DECIDED BY THE ARITHMETIC RATHER THAN THE GLYPH: p5 row 11 (Clay Jensen) renders as '2500' at 1200 dpi with no visible decimal point, but only 25.00 lets p5's own printed subtotal close at 3,014.00 — see that row's note.
